a07cb07f-c7f5-4cb0-a4be-b64f3b002ff4.body:
Choosing between Flutter and React Native for a startup MVP dictates whether you launch in 6 weeks or burn your seed round debugging native bridges. At TechFiyr, we build production apps daily for clients across the US and Europe, and the framework choice always hinges on performance predictability, team skill sets, and CI/CD overhead.

## Why do startups struggle to choose between Flutter and React Native?

Founders often default to what their web developers already know, which usually means React Native because of JavaScript. However, JavaScript bridge overhead frequently causes frame drops on lower-end Android devices. Flutter compiles directly to ARM machine code via the Dart C/C++ runtime, rendering every pixel through its own Skia or Impeller graphics engine. If your MVP requires smooth 60fps animations or heavy local state computation right out of the gate, Flutter wins the technical argument.

When you work with our team at TechFiyr, we evaluate your product requirements against real-world constraints. You can [explore our shipped mobile apps](/projects) to see how we handle cross-platform performance in production.

## How do Flutter and React Native compare on MVP development cost?

| Metric | Flutter (Dart) | React Native (JavaScript/TypeScript) | Verdict |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Initial Setup Time** | 2-3 days | 3-5 days | Flutter wins slightly |
| **UI Consistency** | Pixel-identical across iOS/Android | Relies on native components (sometimes drift) | Flutter wins |
| **Third-Party Packages** | pub.dev (stable, Google-backed) | npm (massive ecosystem, varying quality) | Tie |
| **Developer Hourly Rates** | $30 - $60 / hr | $30 - $60 / hr | Tie |
| **Total MVP Cost (8 Weeks)** | $12,000 - $25,000 | $12,000 - $25,000 | Tie |

The raw cost of hiring developers in Dhaka or partnering with our agency is roughly equivalent for both stacks. The cost savings with Flutter materialize later during maintenance. Because Flutter controls every pixel, you rarely spend billable hours fixing platform-specific UI bugs on older Android versions.

## What is the actual release timeline for an MVP?

A standard startup MVP takes between **4 to 8 weeks** from kickoff to TestFlight and Google Play Console internal testing. Here is how the timeline breaks down for a typical project:

*   **Weeks 1-2:** Architecture setup, state management configuration (Bloc or Riverpod for Flutter; Redux Toolkit or Zustand for React Native), and API contracts.
*   **Weeks 3-5:** Core feature implementation, local secure storage setup, and Firebase/AWS integration.
*   **Weeks 6-7:** Automated CI/CD pipeline setup using Codemagic or GitHub Actions with Fastlane.
*   **Week 8:** Beta testing via TestFlight and Google Play, bug fixing, and App Store submission.

## How difficult is CI/CD setup for Flutter vs React Native?

Automating your release pipeline is mandatory for an MVP so you can push hotfixes without manual terminal commands. 

For Flutter, Codemagic is practically plug-and-play. You connect your repository, configure your provisioning profiles for iOS and keystores for Android, and your build runs smoothly. React Native requires configuring Metro bundler, CocoaPods for iOS, and Gradle for Android, which introduces more points of failure during automated Fastlane builds.

```yaml
# Sample Codemagic workflow snippet for Flutter MVP
workflows:
  flutter-release:
    name: Flutter Automatic Release
    environment:
      flutter: stable
      xcode: latest
    scripts:
      - name: Install dependencies
        script: flutter pub get
      - name: Run unit tests
        script: flutter test
      - name: Build APK and App Bundle
        script: flutter build appbundle --release
```

## Which stack should your startup choose?

Choose Flutter if you want guaranteed UI consistency across low-end and high-end devices, simpler CI/CD pipelines, and fewer native bridge crashes. Choose React Native if your team consists entirely of senior TypeScript developers who can build custom native modules without friction.

Building a minimum viable product requires balancing speed, architectural longevity, and budget. At TechFiyr in Mirpur DOHS, Dhaka, we build production-grade mobile apps and SaaS platforms for clients across the US and Europe. When founders ask us about the real financial commitment required to launch a product, we skip the fluff and look at the actual engineering hours. Read on to see our pricing breakdown, or [explore our shipped mobile apps](/projects) to review our production track record.

## Why choose Flutter for an MVP in 2026?

Flutter remains our primary tool for cross-platform apps because it compiles directly to native ARM machine code using the Dart language. Unlike JavaScript-bridge frameworks, Flutter gives you true 60fps (and 120fps on modern ProMotion displays) UI performance without the jank. For a startup, writing one UI codebase means you launch on both the Apple App Store and Google Play Store simultaneously, cutting your QA and feature-parity cycles in half.

Here is how a typical budget breaks down across engineering phases:

| Project Phase | Estimated Cost (USD) | Timeline | Deliverables |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **UI/UX & Architecture** | $3,500 - $7,000 | 1 - 2 weeks | Figma wireframes, design system, state management plan |
| **Frontend (Flutter/Dart)** | $8,000 - $20,000 | 3 - 5 weeks | Cross-platform views, offline caching, local state |
| **Backend & APIs** | $5,000 - $12,000 | 2 - 4 weeks | Node.js/Go or Firebase, auth, database, REST/GraphQL |
| **CI/CD & App Store Launch** | $1,500 - $3,000 | 1 week | Automated builds, TestFlight, Play Console release |

## How does UI/UX design impact your Flutter MVP budget?

Skimping on UI/UX design guarantees high user churn. We design using atomic design principles in Figma, making sure your widgets map cleanly to Flutter's native layout engine. A standard MVP needs 10 to 25 core screens. Spending 1 to 2 weeks here prevents expensive rewrites during the coding phase. We establish a robust design system early, defining typography, color tokens, and custom widget atoms.

## What drives the cost of the Flutter frontend?

The frontend cost scales with state management complexity and hardware integrations. If your app simply consumes REST endpoints and displays lists, development moves fast using Riverpod or Bloc for state management. However, integrating Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), WebSockets for real-time chat, or complex offline-first SQLite synchronization adds engineering hours.

```dart
// Example of clean Riverpod state management in our Flutter MVPs
final userProvider = StateNotifierProvider<UserNotifier, UserState>((ref) {
  return UserNotifier(ref.watch(authRepositoryProvider));
});
```

## How much should you budget for backend and infrastructure?

Your backend choices dictate your recurring cloud costs and initial development speed. For rapid MVPs, we often deploy serverless architectures using Firebase or Supabase to handle authentication, Firestore/PostgreSQL databases, and edge functions. For clients requiring custom business logic or heavy data processing, we spin up containerized Node.js or Go microservices deployed on AWS via Docker.

## How do automated CI/CD pipelines prevent App Store rejection?

Manual deployment wastes engineering hours and introduces human error. We configure automated CI/CD pipelines using Codemagic or GitHub Actions combined with Fastlane. Every push to main runs unit and widget tests, bumps version numbers, and pushes builds directly to Apple TestFlight and Google Play Internal Testing tracks.
